Both OBP-801 and (R)-Atrochrysone are known to interact with the synaptic vesicular amine transporter, indicating a potential pathway through which Acerogenin B may influence this transporter. The shared involvement of Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase as a common target in both pathways supports a possible mechanism of action involving this enzyme. The integration of these targets highlights a possible role for Acerogenin B in modulating synaptic vesicle function through a series of molecular interactions, though the exact nature of the interaction between Acerogenin B and the transporter remains to be fully elucidated.
